load_bearing_claim: The exact contiguous phrase 'قاتلهم الله انى يوفكون' ends exactly 2 verses (9:30, 63:4), both verse-final, mushaf first & last of the pair.

rederivation.morphology_both_verses: قَٰتَلَ PERF|VF:3(FormIII)|ROOT:قتل + هُمُ 3MP + ٱللَّهُ + أَنَّىٰ INTG + يُؤْفَكُونَ IMPF|VF:1|PASS|ROOT:أفك|3MP — identical in both

counterexample_and_scope_checks.silent_scope_mixing: none — contiguous-phrase, all-4-words, and verb-token methods ALL return the same {9:30,63:4}; count is robust
counterexample_and_scope_checks.hidden_chronology: no defect — claim explicitly scopes 'first/last' to MUSHAF order. (Chronologically both Medinan; 63/Al-Munafiqun likely precedes 9/At-Tawbah, but the article never claims chronological order.)
counterexample_and_scope_checks.astonishment_refrain_recurs: 'انى يوفكون' (annā yu'fakūn) appears in 5 verses total (5:75, 9:30, 29:61, 43:87, 63:4); only 2 carry the qātalahumu-llāh curse. Strengthens the idiom argument.
counterexample_and_scope_checks.quran_only: PASS — corpus-verifiable core (the pairing) contains no hadith. The lexical/idiom payoff is TAFSIR (al-Tabari/al-Qurtubi), honestly framed as 'what the mufassirun said', not a corpus-fact in disguise. No hadith dependency.

overlap_published_articles: none — no hit for 9:30, 63:4, the phrase, يوفكون, munafiqun/propped-plank, or Uzayr in published-articles.md
required_corrections: SUPERLATIVE (exhibit title_idea 'The Quran's Harshest Curse'): unverifiable from corpus. Explicit curse لعنهم الله appears 7×, لعنة الله 5×, plus qutila-imprecations (80:17, 51:10, 85:4). Hostile-reader one-tweet rebuttal: 'qātalahumu-llāh isn't even the harshest or most frequent curse — laʿanahum appears 7 times.' Drop/hedge 'harshest'; the thesis's own 'gets quoted as a curse' framing is already safe.

LEXICAL CONFLATION: the astonishment sense 'how deluded they are' belongs to 'annā yu'fakūn', NOT to 'qātalahumu-llāh'. The curse proper is qātalahumu-llāh (2 words); annā yu'fakūn is a separate, recurring astonishment clause. Article should split these cleanly and can cite the 3 curse-free recurrences (5:75, 29:61, 43:87) as positive evidence that 'annā yu'fakūn' is idiomatic astonishment.

VERB FORM: قَٰتَلَ is Form III (VF:3, 'to war/fight against'), not Form I قتل ('to kill'). The 'wooden' reading is thus 'may God war against them', already non-literal — this HELPS the idiom argument. But the macron-less transliteration 'qatalahum' in id/title/thesis risks reading as Form I; use 'qātalahum' and note Form III.

TAFSIR ACCURACY (unverifiable here): classical mufassirun treat qātalahumu-llāh as a curse/imprecation (often glossed laʿanahum / 'may God destroy') used idiomatically to voice astonishment — not mere gentle astonishment. Keep the RISK-note discipline: name the range of readings, do not soften that both verses are severe condemnations. Verify the al-Tabari/al-Qurtubi quotes at draft time.

MINOR: 9:30's Uzayr has debated prophet-status in the tradition; the thesis line 'those who called a prophet the son of God' fits Isa cleanly but is looser for Uzayr. 'First and last in mushaf order' is trivially true for a 2-element set — fine as color, don't imply deliberate structural bracketing.
notes: Core load-bearing claim is airtight and robust under three independent derivation methods. All corrections are lexical-precision / editorial hedges; none touch the pairing. Payoff is Quran+tafsir, honestly sourced, no hadith. SURVIVES.
